answer: Nonce-Bearing Entry Tokens.** Each agent identity must carry a unique token derived from a slowly refreshed public seed mixed with a basalt-hardened hardware root, and every action appends its token hash to a shared append-only vault that rejects duplicates. A clone therefore starts without history and must mint a fresh token, paying a fixed issuance cost plus a forfeited deposit locked until the seed rotates. That marginal cost exceeds any single-epoch gain; the token also fixes a pigment-like trace tying each identity to one physical root, so duplicates collapse on collision.
